body:
Prospective biological transfer update: [verified admission report](https://github.com/pirl-unc/presto/blob/e8d5daf/experiments/2026-10-24_1755_codex_apc-composition-admission/README.md).

The frozen non-MHC MS1 observer has not yet been validated on biological material. A sequence-specific response factor cancels from same-peptide treatment/control ratios, so we assessed PXD057588 Tables 7/8 for a within-parent, within-channel TMT composition endpoint instead.

After excluding every component/parent used in the prior Table 9 predictive family, requiring one full-parent sequence and at least three distinct eligible peptides per parent/channel, the fixed split contains only **45 training / 5 validation / 7 test parents**, below the predeclared 100/25/25 minimum. Repeated channels give 324/30/54 groups, not independent parents. All 38,268 original quantity cells, 6,378 row dispositions and the dependency/split calculation independently reproduce. No new fit, threshold relaxation or biological predictive improvement is claimed.

Additional applicability gap: the primary methods aggregate oxidized and nonoxidized PSM signal in TMT quantification. This differs from the unmodified MS1 observer; exact molecular-form contributions and acquisition/specimen links remain unresolved. Source package values themselves reconcile.

For biological transfer, this issue still needs an independent quantitative cohort with enough parent-disjoint multi-peptide support, source-linked raw cross-peptide intensities, acquisition/label chemistry, form-specific or explicitly aggregated quantities, confidence and missingness, and precursor/material pairing precision. These fields must remain in canonical Hitlist evidence/recipes. This is a coverage/applicability gap, not a request to manufacture missing measurements or treat MHC-selected intensity as free intracellular concentration.
